notes: Cheapest and fastest run of all 6, and found a genuinely new fact neither the skill run nor our earlier manual investigation had surfaced this explicitly.

Assertion pass rate is NOT the interesting signal this round -- both configurations score similarly (0.88 vs 0.93) because the written assertions didn't anticipate the actual differentiators. Read the per-eval notes, not just the aggregate delta.

nbsphinx eval: baseline (no skill) found the standout result of the whole round -- a real, reproducible crash in the old dependency version against current Sphinx -- by naturally comparing old vs new. The with-skill run, despite following every phase correctly, missed it because Phase 3/4 only verify the NEW version works, never checking whether the OLD one was already broken. This is a design gap to fix before iteration 2, not noise.

pypi-publish eval: with-skill run found the deepest single finding of the round (password-auth now hard-fails per PyPI's 2FA mandate, via actual runtime-script tracing) but dropped the simple 'recommend a TestPyPI dry run' step that baseline included -- source-level proof and an empirical dry-run recommendation should be additive, not substitutes.

ruff eval: both runs performed well and found complementary facts (with-skill: empirical rule-code diff; baseline: the manifest pin is disconnected from what CI actually installs) -- a case where running BOTH configurations, not just one, produced more coverage than either alone.

With-skill runs cost ~33% more tokens and ~44% more wall time on average, but that gap is inflated by the pypi-publish run's much deeper runtime-script tracing (113k tokens vs the ~76k average) -- not a fixed skill overhead.
No silent caps applied: all 3 evals were run at full depth per the skill's per-eval right-sizing judgment, not sampled or truncated.
